trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic personal information, which includes Social Security, passport, and bank account numbers, and geolocation, with a name) of individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected individual in Florida, by mail or email; notice must give the date or date range, the information involved, and a farm contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - workers, employees, and online customers in Florida

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with a synopsis, the number affected, services offered, a copy of the notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Floridians (the online customer list alone is about 2,400)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 are notified

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the farm reasonably determines the breach will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides; the farm will not rely on it when Social Security, passport, or bank account numbers were taken with names (farm policy)

obligation: Law enforcement delay of individual notice
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in its written request
notify: Hold notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the farm (inbound)
trigger: A breach of a system kept by a third-party agent (payroll provider; e-commerce vendor)
deadline: Agent must notify the farm no later than 10 days after its determination; the farm then gives the notices above
notify: The farm (security lead registered as breach contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track with the payroll provider and e-commerce vendor

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected online customers who live outside Florida; H-2A workers now at home-country addresses
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law; workers abroad notified by farm policy in Spanish
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of every affected person

obligation: H-2A earnings statements and records during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: Payroll or field tally unavailable during the incident
deadline: Earnings statement on or before each payday; records made available within 72 hours of a DOL request when kept at a central office
notify: Each H-2A worker (statement); Department of Labor (on request)

obligation: Produce Safety records on FDA request during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: FDA requests records while SYS-01 or the farm network is unavailable
deadline: Readily available; 24 hours for records kept offsite

trigger: Determination that an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 24 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No for the farm - the duty is on a responsible party, the person who registers a food facility (350f(a)(1)); the farm registers none. If tampering (for example fertigation) may have affected shipped produce, tell the distributor at once so it can assess its own duty

obligation: Distributor notice of events affecting food safety or supply
citation: Supplier agreement with the wholesale distributor (contract)
trigger: Any event that could affect product safety, lot traceability, or committed volumes
deadline: Within 24 hours of the farm becoming aware (contract term)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, food and agriculture entities are covered only above the SBA size standard (the farm is below it) and there is no agriculture sector criterion. Recheck when final

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 or field office); CISA reporting
deadline: As soon as practical (Day 0-2 in the runbook)
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and investigation

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring any vendor)

trigger: Suspected compromise of card data or the farm stand terminals
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data or terminals are involved; card data does not enter farm systems

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the farm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
